newsitem.title: USA: Brazil to press on with reform agenda - Malan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to press on with reform agenda - Malan.

text.p: Brazil's Finance Minister Pedro Malan said his country's municipal elections revolved around local issues and the central government would press on with its reform agenda through privatization and fiscal discipline.

The Brazilians Congress should get back to business this week after voters cast ballots last Thursday for about 5,500 mayors and 60,000 council posts, and Malan said the elections were not a referendum on national policies.
"I don't see any wider political or national significance to the outcome of the municipal elections," Malan told reporters after addressing a conference here.

"They were mostly fought on the basis of local, not national or international, issues," he added. "Most of the votes seem to have shown that the incumbent mayors seem to have had an influential effect on getting support for their candidates." With the elections over, Congress seemed likely to focus attention on the issue of approving a consitutional amendment that would allow Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term in office.
Malan said he generally agreed with comments by Brazil's Planning Minister Antonio Kandir last week that approval of the reelection amendment could help sustain economic growth.

"What Kandir said, and he's damn right, is that this reduces the level of uncertainty, of unpredictablitity, if people know there is a possibility of the current president running," Malan said. "It enlarges the time horizon in which decisions are taken and could be a positive thing."
Malan, in a speech before a Wall Street Journal conference here, said the government would continue to press for fiscal reform and vowed to keep a firm grip on inflation.
"In public enterprises, the name of the game is privatization," he said. "On social security we will continue to push for reform."
The minister outlined the government's three goals as reducing inflation, building sustained growth and decreasing the level of social injustice.
